title: Test the Cipher
body:
Goal: write tests for the Caesar cipher from week 5, so nobody can break it without you noticing.

  1. Read cipher_tools.py. It is correct: do not change it.
  2. Open starter.py (YOUR test file) and press Run. pytest shows one line per test with PASSED or FAILED.
  3. TODO 1 test that letters wrap round after z. Use your paper cipher wheel to work out the expected answer.
  4. TODO 2 test that spaces and symbols like ! stay the same.
  5. TODO 3 write one more test of your own.
  6. Press Run: every test should say PASSED.

Done looks like: at least 3 tests, all PASSED.

Remember: if a test fails on the correct encode(), the TEST is wrong. Check your expected answer with the wheel.

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Read the top of cipher_tools.py. It shows what encode() does when letters wrap round and when there are spaces or symbols. Your cipher wheel can check each answer.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: Each test needs an assert line that calls encode() and compares the result to the answer you worked out by hand. Use == to compare. Strings go inside quotes, so the secret message does too.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Shape to fill in: assert encode("____", 3) == "____", "message". For the wrap test, work out where x, y and z land after moving 3 places. For the symbols test, include a space and a ! in the message and check that they stay put.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
"""MY TESTS for encode()  -  this file is YOUR test file.

Read cipher_tools.py first to see what encode() should do.
You can check your expected answers with the paper cipher wheel from week 5!
Press the green Run button to run your tests with pytest.
"""

from cipher_tools import encode


def test_normal_word_shift_1():
    # Normal case: every letter moves one place along.
    assert encode("abc", 1) == "bcd", "a->b, b->c, c->d"


def test_wraps_round_after_z():
    # TODO 1 (edge case): letters near the end of the alphabet must wrap
    #         round to the start. Use the wheel to work out encode("xyz", 3).
    pass


def test_spaces_and_symbols_stay_the_same():
    # TODO 2 (edge case): a message with a space and a ! in it.
    pass


# TODO 3: one more test of your own. Ideas: shift 0 (nothing changes),
#         or an empty message "".


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import pytest
    pytest.main(["-v", __file__])
